messages.subject: Gamma distribution prior and fucntions
parts:
Dear R-INLA discussion group

I have fitted a Gamma distributed (log link) spatiotemporal autoregressive model to fisheries data with formula 

Catch  ~ Year + Soak(rw2) + Gear2 + offset (log(Effort)) + f(lat,long~Year , model="ar1") #Used pc.priors for the GMRF and the smooth effect. 

When inspecting the residuals from this model against the fitted values, one can observe a decrease in variability with increasing mean (see attached). As far as I was aware, it is usual that the Gamma variance increases with the mean, but I am obtaining the opposite. 

This pattern is observed particularly when plotting the residuals against the covariate "Soak" and "Gear2". 

One colleague suggested I could perhaps include either "Soak"/"Gear2" as a covariate of the gamma precision/scale parameter. This way it would accommodate better the pattern in the residuals I am observing. 

As far I have read, the Gamma distribution is defined by a parameter φ, which have a loggamma prior (1,0.01), but I have not been able to find any examples of how could I modify the shape of the gamma distribution to better accommodate my data or to define it from a covariate as suggested.

Any help or literature would be greatly appreciated. 

Regards

Guillermo

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Gamma distribution prior and fucntions
parts:
Hi,

I'm afraid there is no implementation of the precision depending on a
covariate for the Gamma. There is 'scale' variable, so if you know the
effect of the covariate, you can set that. You can also use the marginal
likelihood to evaluate different choice for that covariate, like in the
work of Virgilio Gómez-Rubio [I think the trick is used in several
papers]

Best
H

Dear H

Thanks for your answer again. 

After changing the 'scale' variable in my model, to the value of the Mean from the Precision of Soak time,
I observe a decrease in the scale of my residuals, but the pattern in still quite obvious as seen in the figure attached. 

From the explanation in ?inla, it says :

scale= "Fixed (optional) scale parameters of the precision for Gaussian and Student-T response models. Default value is rep(1, n.data)"

I assume it also applies to the gamma? 

Another question that came to my head after reading this. Would I expect the same changes from modifying the 'scale' variable than from defining a new prior for the precision parameter of the Gamma distribution?  As both are referring to the precision?

Thanks

G

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Gamma distribution prior and fucntions
parts:
Hi,

yes, for this you have check the documentation

inla.doc("gamma")

and you see how 'scale' s is defined.

> Another question that came to my head after reading this. Would I
> expect the same changes from modifying the 'scale' variable than from
> defining a new prior for the precision parameter of the Gamma
> distribution? As both are referring to the precision?
>

yes, this is like every observation can have different scale.

In the gaussian case, its like

Prec(y_i) = \tau * s_i

so \tau is common, and the scale s_i is a constant for each i.

H
